content: To revert a page means to undo all changes made to it after a specific point in time, effectively restoring the page to its previous state as it existed at that earlier time. A partial revert, on the other hand, undoes only some of the changes made after that point. To revert a page to an earlier version, follow these steps: 1. Navigate to the page you wish to revert. Click on the History tab located at the top of the page. From the list of revisions, click on the time and date of the earlier version you want to restore. Note that clicking on options like cur, last, or Compare selected versions will not work for this purpose. 2. Once the earlier version of the page is displayed, you will see text similar to (Revision as of 23:19, Jul 15, 2003) below the page title. This replaces the usual From {project name} text. 3. Verify that the displayed version is the correct one you wish to revert to. Then, click the link to edit the page as you normally would. 4. When editing, you will see a warning above the edit box indicating that you are editing an outdated revision. Ignore this warning and proceed to save the page. 5. In the edit summary, make sure to include the word revert (or rv) to indicate the action you have taken. Reverts and Edit Conflicts Reverting a page does not cause an edit conflict. If someone else edits the page between the time you press edit and post, their edits will be silently overwritten. However, their changes will still be recorded in the page history. Be cautious when reverting high-traffic pages, as this can lead to unintended overwrites. If it appears that someone has deleted your edits, consider whether it might be an unfortunate case of revision conflict rather than intentional deletion. Admin-Only Rollback Link On a user contributions page, administrators have access to additional rollback links for contributions marked as the most recent edit (the last edit made by anyone to that article). The diff page, which shows the differences between an old and the current version of a page, also includes this link. Clicking the rollback link reverts the page to the last version not made by the user being reverted. This feature is particularly useful when dealing with known vandals, as their edits can be reverted without needing to review them first. An automatic edit summary, such as Reverted edits by X to last version by Y, is added when this feature is used. However, this feature cannot be used if the last two edits were made by the same user and you want to revert to an earlier version. Additionally, if someone else edits or rolls back the page between the time you load the User Contributions page and press rollback, a message saying Rollback failed will appear, explaining the issue. If the page was created by a malicious user and no one else has edited it, clicking the rollback link will result in the message Cannot revert edit; last contributor is only author of this article. In such cases, the appropriate action is to delete the page.
